title: A History of American Manufactures from 1608 to 1860: Comprising Annals of the Industry of the United States in Machinery, Manufactures and Useful Arts, with a Notice of the Important Inventions, Tariffs, and the Results of Each Decennial Census
note: Volume 1 of 3. The first issue of v.1 appeared in 1861; Bishop entrusted the completion of the work to Edwin T. Freedley in 1862, and this is a later issue of that first volume. Includes bibliographical references.

title: Catalogue of the Works Exhibited in the British Section of the Exhibition: In French and English, Together with Exhibitors' Prospectuses, Prices Current, &c
note: British section catalogue for the 1855 Paris Universal Exposition, issued in parallel English and French versions. Together with the 1867 and 1878 catalogues, part of the documentary record of British industrial exports.

title: Official Catalogue of the British Section
authors: Great Britain. Royal Commission for the Paris Exhibition
note: Part 2 only. Issued for the Royal Commission for the Paris Universal International Exhibition of 1878; head of title reads "Paris universal international exhibition, 1878". Printed by G. E. Eyre and W. Spottiswoode for H.M. Stationery Office (LCCN 05031735).

title: Catalogue of the British Section: Containing a List of the Exhibitors of the United Kingdom and Its Colonies, and the Objects Which They Exhibit
authors: Exposition universelle de 1867 à Paris. Section britannique
note: British section catalogue for the 1867 Paris Universal Exposition, printed in four languages, with statistical introductions and an appendix describing many of the exhibited objects more fully. The volume also contains an introduction to the catalogue and an illustrations section.

title: British Industries: A Series of General Reviews for Business Men and Students
note: Lectures delivered during the winter of 1902-3 under the auspices of the University of Birmingham, by Sir William Ashley, opening with the British iron and steel industries. Bibliographic note from the volume states the lectures date from 1902-03 while the imprint is 1907.

title: Industrial Germany
note: 274 pp., in the public domain. Digitised by the Digital Library of India from the North Bengal State Library, Coochbehar; indexed under the subject headings "Technology" and "Various industries, trades and crafts". A pre-war account of German industrial development, read alongside Howard (1907) in this set.

title: From Domestic Manufacture to Industrial Revolution: The Case of the Rhineland Textile Districts
note: ISBN 0-19-505111-4 (LCCN 88025415). Kisch (1924-1978) died before completing the work; the manuscript was published posthumously, first in German in 1981 as Die hausindustriellen Textilgewerbe am Niederrhein vor der industriellen Revolution (Max-Planck-Institut für Geschichte, Band 65, Göttingen: Vandenhoeck & Ruprecht). The linked PDF is a freely downloadable copy held in community-uploaded item 32879168; the canonical archive.org item fromdomesticmanu0000kisc is access-restricted (borrow-only).
source_file: archive.org item 32879168, file "From domestic manufacture to Industrial Revolution.pdf"

title: The Cause and Extent of the Recent Industrial Progress of Germany
note: Bibliography at pp. [xi]-xiii. Subject headings include "Working class — Germany", "Industries — Germany", and "Germany — Economic conditions"; the book treats the causes of German industrialisation and the working-class response to it.

title: British Manufacturing Industries
note: Volume 1 of a large multi-volume series edited by G. Phillips Bevan. Bibliographic caveats recorded on the item: vol. 10 is wanting in the Library of Congress set; vols. 13-14 carry the title The industrial classes and industrial statistics; later volumes have variant titles. This record covers volume 1 only.
